misconceptions.description: Treating a confident, well-written AI answer as factually correct without checking it
misconceptions.trigger: learner accepts an AI claim because it sounds authoritative
misconceptions.feedback: Fluency is not accuracy. Verify each factual claim against a trustworthy source before you use it.

misconceptions.description: Using a source, author, or link the AI produced without confirming it actually exists
misconceptions.trigger: learner cites an AI-generated reference without opening or finding it
misconceptions.feedback: Open every AI-supplied citation. If you cannot find the real source, do not use the claim or the citation.

misconceptions.description: Writing a one-line prompt with no role, task, format, or constraints and expecting a usable result
misconceptions.trigger: learner submits a broad prompt like 'write about technology'
misconceptions.feedback: State the role, the task, the audience, and the format. Specific prompts make the output easier to verify and revise.
